method: OPEN AND QUOTED from Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3) 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)' (published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023)). Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at NCBI PMC efetch JATS <license> element for PMC10425483 (Europe PMC returned HTTP 503 on 2026-09-23)).

claims.claim: **SCLC is about 15% of lung cancers; most present at extensive stage.** Smoking is the main risk factor, and 10–20% have brain metastases at diagnosis.
claims.source_text: SCLC accounts for approximately 15% of all lung cancer diagnoses … More than two-thirds of all cases are diagnosed in extensive-stage (ES) … with approximately 10-20% of patients presenting with brain metastases (BM) at the initial diagnosis … Smoking is known to be the primary risk factor for SCLC
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnose on WHO criteria, preferring histology to cytology.** PD-L1 testing is not routinely recommended; no predictive biomarker is validated.
claims.source_text: The pathological diagnosis of SCLC should be made using the World Health Organization (WHO) classification (IV, A) []. Histology is preferred over cytology (V, A). … Not predictive biomarker has been validated in clinical practice and PD-L1 testing is not routinely recommended.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Rule out neurological paraneoplastic syndromes before immunotherapy**, because immunotherapy can worsen them.
claims.source_text: The presence of neurologic paraneoplastic syndromes that can be aggravated by immunotherapy must be ruled out (V, C).
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stage with contrast CT of chest and abdomen plus brain MRI** (CT if MRI is impossible). PET-CT is recommended in limited stage to plan thoracic radiotherapy.
claims.source_text: Full staging includes computed tomography (CT) scan (with intravenous contrast) of the chest/abdomen and brain imaging by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or CT scan (if MRI is not possible) (III, A). … is recommended in patients with LS to assist thoracic radiotherapy in localized tumor (III, A)
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Limited stage** is disease confined to one hemithorax and regional nodes that can be treated with definitive chemoradiation (stage I–III); **extensive stage** is disease beyond that (stage IV).
claims.source_text: LS is defined as the tumor being confined to one hemithorax and regional lymph nodes (stage I-III; T any, N any, M0), that can be treated with definitive chemoradiation therapy. … ES defines disease outside of the thorax or not accessible for radiation therapy (stage IV; T any, N any, M1a/b/c; or T3-4 due to multiple lung nodules)
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stage I–IIA (node-negative, under 5% of cases): lobectomy with lymph-node dissection after mediastinal staging, then adjuvant cisplatin–etoposide.** PCI is not recommended in this subgroup.
claims.source_text: Treatment recommendations for stages I-IIA (T1-2, N0, M0), which represent fewer than 5% of all SCLC, include surgery after mediastinal staging … Lobectomy with a systematic lymph-node dissection is the preferred surgical procedure (II, A). … Adjuvant combination of cisplatin plus etoposide is recommended as systemic treatment in stage I-IIA (IV, A). … Therefore, PCI is not recommended in this subgroup of patients (II, E).
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Stage IIB–IIIC: concurrent chemoradiation followed by PCI.** Cisplatin–etoposide for up to four cycles; carboplatin only when cisplatin is contraindicated. Avoid dose reductions, especially in the first two cycles.
claims.source_text: Treatment recommendation for such stages (T1-T4, N0-N3, M0) is cCRT (I, A) followed by PCI (I, A). … ChT should be recommended up to four cycles (II, B) []. Carboplatin should be reserved only when cisplatin is contraindicated (II, A) … ChT dose reduction should be avoided, especially during the first two cycles
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Thoracic radiotherapy: 45 Gy in 30 twice-daily fractions of 150 cGy over 3 weeks**; 60–70 Gy once daily if twice-daily is not possible. Start with chemotherapy cycle 1 or 2.
claims.source_text: The optimal dose and fractionation in LS-SCLC is 45 Gy delivered in 30 twice-daily fractions of 150 cGy over 3 weeks (I, A). … For patients unable to undergo twice-daily treatment, daily RT of 60-70 Gy is an acceptable alternative (II, A) … earlier TRT is superior to delayed RT and should start with ChT cycle 1 or 2.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PCI 25 Gy in 10 daily fractions** for responders to chemoradiation with PS 0–1. Share the decision when PS is 2, age is over 70, or there is pre-existing neurological disease; hippocampal-avoidance PCI is a reasonable alternative.
claims.source_text: PCI is currently offered to patients who respond to initial cCRT and have a PS of 0-1. The recommended dose is 25 Gy in 10 daily fractions (I, A) … The evidence supporting PCI is not as clear in patients with a post-cCRT PS of 2, in patients > 70 years of age and in those with pre-existing neurological conditions. In such cases, a shared decision process should be encouraged (IV, B). … it is reasonable to offer HA-PCI as an alternative to standard PCI (II, B).
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sequential chemoradiation** is an option when poor PS, comorbidity or disease volume rules out concurrent treatment; concurrent treatment can be standard for fit older patients.
claims.source_text: Sequential CRT is an option for individuals who are not considered eligible for cCRT due to poor PS, comorbidities, and/or disease volume (V, B) … cCRT could be considered the standard treatment for fit elderly patients (IV, B)
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **First line: platinum–etoposide plus atezolizumab or durvalumab** for untreated patients with ECOG PS 0–1 and controlled brain metastases, including older patients; carboplatin is preferred over cisplatin in the elderly.
claims.source_text: Therefore, all patients with advanced SCLC with ECOG PS 0-1, controlled BM, and no previous treatment should be offered the combination of standard ChT plus atezolizumab or durvalumab (I,A). … For elderly ES-SCLC patients, carboplatin/etoposide regimen is preferred than cisplatin/etoposide (I, B) … Atezolizumab and durvalumab combined with ChT are recommended as the first-line treatment for elderly patients with ES-SCLC (I, B)
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The trials gave four cycles of chemo-immunotherapy, then maintenance immunotherapy until progression.** Median survival rose to 12.3 months (atezolizumab) and 12.9 months (durvalumab). PS 2 or worse was not studied.
claims.source_text: added to carboplatin plus etoposide for four cycles, followed by maintenance atezolizumab or placebo until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or patient withdrawal. The two co-primary endpoints, OS and PFS, were met. Median OS was 12.3 months for atezolizumab … platinum plus etoposide and durvalumab, with or without tremelimumab, for four cycles, followed by maintenance durvalumab; ChT for up to six cycles in the control arm was allowed. In the comparison between ChT alone and the durvalumab arm, mOS of 12.9 months was observed for durvalumab plus ChT … Patients with PS ≥ 2 were not included in these trials and the use of ChT-IO upfront has not been established.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consolidative thoracic radiotherapy (30 Gy in 10 fractions)** is an option for PS 0–2 patients with residual thoracic disease who respond to first-line treatment.
claims.source_text: Thus, in patients with PS of 0-2 who achieve a response after ChT, TRT to the residual tumor and lymph nodes (30 Gy/10 fractions) is a treatment option (II, B). … 30 Gy of TRT can be safely administered to these patients with residual thoracic disease after the completion of ChT-IO (V, C).
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PCI in extensive stage is controversial;** MRI surveillance is an alternative, and is preferred in older patients because of neurocognitive risk.
claims.source_text: Therefore, for patients who can adhere to the schedule, MRI surveillance can be contemplated as an alternative to PCI. … Active CNS surveillance other than PCI is preferred in older patients with ES-SCLC (I, A)
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider a clinical trial for every relapse.** Relapse more than 3 months after platinum: rechallenge with platinum–etoposide. Otherwise topotecan (oral or IV), or CAV.
claims.source_text: All cases of relapsed SCLC should be assessed for inclusion in a clinical trial. … For sensitive patients whose disease has relapsed or progress after 3 months after completion of first-line treatment, rechallenge with platinum-etoposide ChT is recommended (II, B). … Oral or i.v. topotecan is recommended for patients with platinum-resistant or -sensitive relapse (I, A), an alternative is the combination of cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin and vincristine (CAV) (II, B)
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PD-1 inhibitor monotherapy is not recommended for relapsed SCLC.**
claims.source_text: PD-1 axis inhibitors have not been approved and cannot be generally recommended as monotherapy for relapsed SCLC.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep chemotherapy dose intensity;** G-CSF prophylaxis is safe in limited stage and an option in extensive stage.
claims.source_text: In SCLC, dose intensity is of paramount importance to achieve better outcomes; therefore, ChT dose reductions should be avoided. … For LS, the use of prophylactic granulocyte or granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factors (G/GM-CSF) has demonstrated to be a safe supportive measure, with no detrimental effect on survival (II, B). … For ES, the use of G/GM-CSF is a treatment option to prevent hematologic toxicity (II, B).
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow-up CT:** limited stage every 3 months for 2 years, 6-monthly in year 3, then yearly; extensive stage every 2–3 months. Without PCI, brain MRI every 3 months in the first year, then 6-monthly.
claims.source_text: For LS-SCLC, after treatment completion, a CT scan is recommended every 3 months for 2 years, then every 6 months during year 3, and then annually (V, C). For ES, after completing initial or subsequent therapy, CT scans every 2-3 months are recommended … MRI (preferred) or CT brain with contrast every 3 months during the first year, then every 6 months thereafter are recommended in patients who did not undergo PCI.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Lung Cancer Group (GECP), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-023-03216-3), 'SEOM-GECP Clinical guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) (2022)', published 7 July 2023 (correction PMC10425482, September 2023), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425483/, retrieved 2026-09-23
